teaser: We teach programming the way Lockhart says we teach maths: concepts first. Explorer coding starts where the hook is.
core_idea: Programming, like maths in Lockhart's lament, is usually taught upside down, concepts before purpose, so people dislike it and return to Excel; what hooks a programmer is control in a short feedback loop, which the good tools always had, and explorer coding by voice now starts at that end, with coding understood as communication whose primitives people will read more, not less.

quotes.text: The thing about programming is the ability to control something: to make something work.
They program wherever the loop is short and the result is theirs.
Coding is communication: speaking to a computer, through an abstraction layer.

figures.caption: Programming, taught upside down. Usually: syntax and types, variables and functions, classes and structure, exercises with no purpose, and often nothing useful at the end. How it is learned: something you want to control, make it work and see it work, the concept you need when you need it, and structure because you need it.

The tools that got the loop right: BASIC on the ZX Spectrum, Visual Basic, the spreadsheet, Scratch, Code Club, and now explorer coding. Each made the distance from an idea to seeing it work very short.
The irony: taught programming with nothing useful to build, people go back to the spreadsheet, and program there anyway. Microsoft calls Excel the world's most widely used programming language.
Coding is communication: voice and briefs, visual blocks, code and its primitives, and the machine underneath. The way in changes; the primitives stay.
